explication:
## Purpose and runtime
OpenComputers is a Minecraft 1.7.10 Forge mod that adds persistent, programmable computers, robots, networks, peripherals, and in-game Lua operating systems. Production code is primarily Scala, with Java APIs and compatibility code. Gradle builds/package the mod: `build.gradle`, `src/main/resources/mcmod.info`.

## Bootstrap and sided entry points
The mod entry class owns lifecycle registration, configuration, proxies, and initialization of blocks/items/recipes. Forge/coremod loading is also used for bytecode transformation. Client, common, and dedicated-server behavior are separated through proxies and packet/GUI handlers.
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/OpenComputers.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/common/Proxy.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/common/launch/TransformerLoader.scala`

## World devices and persisted state
Minecraft blocks, items, tile entities, inventories, and templates model the physical computer ecosystem. Tile entities are the server-authoritative persisted runtime hosts; item data represents portable/configurable hardware. Cases, racks, robots, drones, screens, adapters, and storage are major concrete hosts.
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/common/tileentity/Case.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/common/tileentity/Robot.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/common/item/data/RobotData.scala`

## Component-network layer
Devices expose nodes, connectors, managed environments, messages, and packets to an internal component graph. Network implementations connect wired, wireless, quantum, and routing/distribution behavior; tile-entity traits bridge world objects into this graph. This is the key boundary between Minecraft placement/topology and programmable components.
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/server/network/Network.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/server/network/WirelessNetwork.scala`
- `src/main/java/li/cil/oc/api/network/Node.java`

## Machine execution and Lua boundary
The server machine runtime schedules persistent virtual computers and invokes component callbacks. It supports native Lua 5.2/JNLua and LuaJ architectures, exposing computer, component, OS, persistence, Unicode, and userdata APIs to guest code. Lua scripts cannot directly operate Minecraft objects; they act through registered component environments and callback wrappers.
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/server/machine/Machine.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/server/machine/luac/NativeLuaArchitecture.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/server/machine/luaj/LuaJLuaArchitecture.scala`

## Drivers, components, and storage
The driver registry discovers item/block implementations and converts them into server-side components. Components implement peripheral semantics—filesystems, GPUs, networking, redstone, inventories, robots, and upgrades. Filesystem abstractions isolate machine-visible storage from resource, stream, virtual, and optional ComputerCraft-backed implementations.
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/server/driver/Registry.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/server/component/FileSystem.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/server/fs/VirtualFileSystem.scala`

## Client/server synchronization and presentation
Server authority sends GUI, component-tracking, and state/render packets; client handlers update GUIs, render tile entities/entities, draw text buffers, and play sounds. Shared packet definitions form the network boundary rather than direct client access to world state.
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/common/PacketBuilder.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/server/PacketHandler.scala`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/client/renderer/tileentity/ScreenRenderer.scala`

## Extensibility and bundled content
A public Java API supports external mods. Optional integration modules conditionally register drivers, converters, power/redstone support, and event hooks for numerous Forge mods. Bundled assets provide BIOS/OpenOS and loot-disk Lua programs, recipes, manuals, localization, models, textures, and sounds.
- `src/api/java/li/cil/oc/api/API.java`
- `src/main/scala/li/cil/oc/integration/Mods.scala`
- `src/main/resources/assets/opencomputers/loot/openos/init.lua`
